**Game of Life – Three Rounds**

Starting from an empty board (no live cells), applying the standard Conway rules for three generations leaves the grid unchanged—there remain zero live cells throughout.  
(An empty board stays empty forever.)

---

### Chess Position After Two Moves  

|   | A | B | C | D | E | F | G | H |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **8** | r | n | b | q | k | b | n | r |
| **7** | p | p | p | p | . | p | p | p |
| **6** | . | . | . | . | . | . | . | . |
| **5** | . | . | . | . | p | . | . | . |
| **4** | . | . | . | . | P | . | . | . |
| **3** | . | . | . | . | . | . | . | . |
| **2** | P | P | P | P | . | P | P | P |
| **1** | R | N | B | Q | K | B | N | R |

*Explanation:*  
- White’s move **e4** advances the pawn from e₂ to e₄.  
- Black responds with **e5**, moving their pawn from e₇ to e₅.  

All other pieces stay in their original positions.
